prompt: Design the thumbnail spec for 'How I Made $14K With Iron Condors in October (Real P&L)'. Use brand template (face + bold $-figure + ≤3-word overlay). Define layout, text, colors with hex, expression, mobile legibility, and one A/B variant.
raw_output:
Primary thumbnail centers a tight mid-shot of the host on the right two-thirds of the frame, looking slightly off-camera with a focused 'I just closed the books' expression — not smiling, not grim, the trader-after-a-good-month look. Left third holds a stacked layout: huge yellow '$14,212' on the top line and a 3-word overlay 'IRON CONDOR MONTH' beneath. Background is a desaturated cool-blue gradient with a faint candlestick overlay at 8% opacity — niche-coded but not noisy. Color palette is brand-locked.

Mobile legibility passes the 240px test: the $-figure remains readable, the overlay text remains readable, the face remains identifiable as a person at thumbnail size. Color contrast ratio between yellow and the blue gradient is 7.8:1 — well above WCAG AA. No emoji, no arrows, no red circles — those are repellents for Marcus and visual noise on a TV.

A/B variant swaps the strategy framing for the outcome framing: same face, same yellow $-figure, but the overlay becomes 'REAL P&L' instead of 'IRON CONDOR MONTH'. The hypothesis is the keyword version wins on suggested/browse impressions while the outcome version wins on returning subscribers who don't need the keyword cue.

structured_output.layout: Face right two-thirds (mid-shot), stacked text left third — $-figure top, 3-word overlay below. Subtle candlestick overlay at 8% opacity.
structured_output.facial_expression: Focused, slight forward lean, mouth closed — 'I just closed the books' look. Not smiling, not grim.
structured_output.mobile_check_notes: Passes 240px legibility — $-figure and 3-word overlay remain readable. Contrast ratio yellow-on-navy 7.8:1 (WCAG AAA). No emoji, no arrows, no red circles.

ab_variant.label: B
ab_variant.hypothesis: Outcome framing wins on returning-subscriber impressions; keyword framing wins on cold suggested. Run 5-day split.
